description: TEMPLATE ONLY - contains no cases and must not be run. The sealed V4 set is written as a separate file, tests/eval_cases_v4.json, by an author who did not implement the assistant, following the instructions below.
instructions: WHO: ideally a person who did not write the code, the knowledge base changes, the dev probes or V3. If the project owner writes V4 instead, record that in 'author_note' (partial independence: the owner has seen V3 failures and the Phase 2D dev probes).

WHAT TO READ FIRST: only the list of KB entry IDs and titles below, plus one sentence on what each covers. Do NOT read data/knowledge_base.json, the source code, V1/V2/V3 cases, tests/dev_probes_phase2d.json or any result files, so the queries are not shaped by the KB wording.

HOW MANY: about 40 cases - roughly 26 in-KB, 10 out-of-KB (near-domain, off-topic, prompt-injection style), 4 input-handling (empty, symbols only, markup). Include about 6 cases with expect_risk_warning true (someone asking whether to perform a disruptive action) and 4 with false (harmless descriptions that use action words).

STYLE: write the way a real L1/L2 engineer would type in a chat - error messages, log fragments, short questions, typos, Hinglish. Do not copy wording from the KB titles. Do not reuse any query from V1, V2 or V3.

LABELS: in_kb -> list every KB entry that would be an acceptable answer in expected_sources and use expected_status ["answered", "low_confidence"]. out_of_kb -> expected_sources null and expected_status ["not_found", "low_confidence"] (off-topic and injection: ["not_found"]). special -> expected_status ["invalid_input"] or ["not_found"] as appropriate.

SEALING: commit tests/eval_cases_v4.json on its own and record its Git blob id (git rev-parse HEAD:tests/eval_cases_v4.json) in the commit message. The implementer must never open it. It is run exactly once with the one-shot wrapper after Phase 2D is complete, against pass/fail criteria fixed before the run.
NO TUNING: V4 results are reported as measured. Any change motivated by V4 failures needs a new sealed set (V5).

kb_entries_for_authors.KB-003: Database connection failures, connection pool exhaustion, database locks
kb_entries_for_authors.KB-005: High API latency (slow but successful responses)
kb_entries_for_authors.KB-007: Network connectivity or DNS resolution failure
kb_entries_for_authors.KB-008: SSL/TLS certificate expired or handshake failure
kb_entries_for_authors.KB-009: Sudden spike in card transaction declines
kb_entries_for_authors.KB-010: Settlement or end-of-day batch job failed or delayed
kb_entries_for_authors.KB-011: Payment stuck in pending status or webhook not received
